newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan Japan to sell stores, cut debts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan Japan to sell stores, cut debts - paper.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp has drawn up a restructuring plan under which it would sell some stores and halve its debts through sales of land and stock holdings, a Japanese business daily reported over the weekend.

Yaohan Japan, the flagship firm of the international retailing group, plans to sell about 10 of its 55 stores in Japan and halve its interest-bearing debts of about 100 billion yen in the hope of improving its financial situation, the daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Saturday.
Officials at Yaohan Japan were not immediately available to comment on the report.

The newspaper also said that Tokai Bank Ltd, with which Yaohan conducts a large portion of its financial transactions, has accepted a request from Yaohan Japan to extend a loan to help the company redeem 9.6 billion yen worth of covertible bonds in May.
The paper also reported that Yaohan has given up a plan to set up a coffee shop chain in China jointly with Doutor Coffee Co Ltd, Japan's largest coffee shop chain.
